interpretive_convention.adopted_definition: Use the nontrivial spectral/common-neighbour convention operational in the source paper: a finite connected noncomplete regular graph with constant adjacent and nonadjacent common-neighbour counts, equivalently a regular graph with exactly three distinct adjacency eigenvalues and valency of multiplicity one.
interpretive_convention.degenerate_imprimitive_cases: graphs with fewer than three distinct eigenvalues, including equal-clique unions and matchings such as 2K4 and 4K2, are excluded
interpretive_convention.caveat: The source paper does not give a standalone definition, but it treats a strongly regular distance graph via three eigenvalues kappa, r, and -s. This source-operational convention supersedes revision 2's literal Wikipedia-only reading.

target_statement: Does there exist a Q-polynomial distance-regular graph Gamma of diameter 3 such that its distance-2 graph Gamma_2 and distance-3 graph Gamma_3 are strongly regular?

source_clauses.text: For a graph Gamma of diameter d and i in {1,...,d}, Gamma_i has the same vertices and joins u,w exactly when their distance in Gamma is i.
Does there exist a Q-polynomial distance-regular graph Gamma of diameter 3 such that Gamma_2 and Gamma_3 are strongly regular?

constraints.statement: The target asks for existence of one graph Gamma satisfying all remaining rows.
Gamma is a Q-polynomial distance-regular graph.
Gamma_i uses the same vertex set as Gamma and adjacency exactly at distance i in Gamma.

Gamma_2 is a nontrivial strongly regular graph in the source-operational sense: it is connected, noncomplete and regular, has constant common-neighbour counts on adjacent and nonadjacent pairs, and has exactly three distinct adjacency eigenvalues.

Gamma_3 is a nontrivial strongly regular graph in the source-operational sense: it is connected, noncomplete and regular, has constant common-neighbour counts on adjacent and nonadjacent pairs, and has exactly three distinct adjacency eigenvalues.
At least one such graph Gamma exists.
